answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays when paths repeatedly encounter poorly connected regions. A sybil cluster may harbor many identities yet typically attaches to honest nodes through a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits walk escape and, by min-cut transitivity bounds, caps the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. Thus each forged identity is not a pearl of independent power, but part of a constrained tundra of mutually reinforcing nodes.
